[ALUSI:92:17/r5] ALUSI, d. 1270 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī calls the restrictions rhetorical hyperbole in a comparison of exemplary leaders among unbelievers and believers, not strict exclusions; al-Kashf praises this, but al-Alūsī notes its Muʿtazilite premise of eternal punishment for major sinners.
[ALUSI:92:17/r6] ALUSI, d. 1270 · القاضي | reports | Al-Qāḍī argues that the indefinite Hell in verse 15 could mean one level, so it need not say only unbelievers enter any Hell; al-Zamakhsharī objects that verse 17 then appears to keep all but the most pious from that level. | mentions 92:15, 92:17
[ALUSI:92:17/r7] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | reports | Al-Qāḍī may reject implication from the description, so verse 17 does not restrict exclusion to the most pious; those who reject such implication avoid most of the conflict.
[ALUSI:92:17/r9] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | reports | Another proposal treats the elatives as ordinary descriptors, a wretched person and a pious person; Ṭarafa uses wāḥid to mean alone, but this does not solve the restriction problem for unbelievers, poor pious people, children, and the mentally ill.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Most reports say the surah was revealed about Abū Bakr, with sound chains from Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and others; al-Suddī instead links it to Abū al-Daḥdāḥ's charitable purchase of a palm for orphans, but that Ibn ʿAbbās report is weak according to al-Suyūṭī.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعض المفسرين | reports | Some say the closing description of the most God-fearing specifically concerns Abū Bakr and report consensus, whereas some Shīʿites claim it concerns ʿAlī; Alusi says the surah details the previous surah's success and failure.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The two exclusions seem in tension if ṣaly means any entry into or heat from Hell: believers who sin are neither the most wretched nor the most pious. Alusi resolves this by reading ṣaly as especially severe torment between Hell's layers. | mentions 92:15, 92:16
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن المنير | reports | Ibn al-Munir transmits lexicographers' description of ṣaly as placing an animal in a pit between layers of gathered coals, supporting the sense of especially intense torment.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari treats the exclusion as rhetorical comparison between an eminent unbeliever and an eminent believer, not a strict exclusion of every other unbeliever or believer; al-Kashf approves, but Alusi notes its Muʿtazilite premise about sinners remaining in Hell.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · القاضي | reports | The Judge argues that “a Fire” is indefinite, so this verse need not say that only unbelievers enter any level of Hell; Hell has different layers. Al-Zamakhshari objects that the next verse still excludes all but the most pious from that Fire. | mentions 92:15, 92:16, 92:17
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | A possible reply is that the Judge rejects the inferential force of descriptive restriction, so this verse does not establish a strict exclusion for him; the phrase “only the most wretched” remains harder to explain. | mentions 92:15, 92:17
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · أبو هريرة | reports | A hadith from Abu Hurayra says only the wretched enter Hell; when asked who is wretched, the Prophet describes one who neither obeys God nor leaves sin for God. Sunnis interpret such reports in light of evidence that grave sinners may be punished.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Another proposed solution takes ashqā and atqā generically as “wretched” and “pious,” citing Tarafa's use of a comparative form to mean “one”; Alusi says this does not resolve the exclusions.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · طرفة | reports | The continuation of Tarafa's line ends “I am not alone in that path”; Alusi says awḥad here means wāḥid, supporting use of comparatives as generic descriptors.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | rejects | Alusi says the generic reading still fails: restricting torment to the unbeliever would imply no other person enters or is punished, against Sunni doctrine; restricting escape to the very pious would exclude sinful believers and even children, the insane, and those without property.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · صاحب الكشف | reports | After weighing the positions, Alusi says one may prefer al-Kashf's approval of al-Zamakhshari's rhetorical reading if one does not hold that grave sinners remain forever in Hell.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Jannaba governs two objects: al-atqā is the first and the Hell-pronoun the second, promoted to subject in the passive; the root means putting to one side and often distancing, as here.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الإمام | reports | The Imam uses these verses to argue that Abū Bakr was the community's best, and says their context rules out the Shīʿī claim that they concern ʿAlī; Alusi notes that the argument is lengthy and disputable.
[ELMALILI:92:12-21/r8] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | The most God-fearing avoids both disbelief and sin, is kept far from the Fire, never enters it, and passes easily onward to Paradise.
[QUTB-ZILAL:92:17/r1] QUTB-ZILAL, d. 1386 · author | holds | The most God-fearing person is the fortunate counterpart of the most wretched person. | mentions 92:15, 92:16
[IBNASHUR:92:15/r11] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Al-ashqā and al-atqā form a near-paronomasia (jinās muḍāriʿ). | mentions 92:17
[IBNASHUR:92:15/r7] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | At the rise of Islam, people fell into two groups, unbelievers or pious believers; converts had embraced Islam wholeheartedly and did not com

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | الأشقى and الأتقى mean the most wretched and most devout in degree, a common intensifying usage.

[TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r4] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · عطاء | reports | A report from ʿAta names the man Abu al-Dahdah; al-Suyuti transmits the story from Ibn ʿAbbas through Ibn Abi Hatim and calls it weak.
[TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · الرازي | reports | Al-Razi says Sunni exegetes agree the “most pious” is Abu Bakr; he says Shia exegetes instead name ʿAli, citing 5:55, and interpret the superlative as the best human. | mentions 5:55
[TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | rejects | The author rejects as an overstatement the claim that all Shia sources name ʿAli; he says the reliable Shia evidence supports Abu al-Dahdah and again rejects an absolute “best of all people” reading. | mentions 5:55
[TABATABAI:92:15-20/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | prefers | The “most pious” means the person more God-fearing than others, including those wary of worldly loss or poverty: among them, the one who spends for God is most pious. The descriptor makes the interpretation general, without excluding a specific occasion of revelation.
[TABATABAI:92:15-20/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | rejects | Making “most pious” and “most wretched” absolute superlatives over all people implies that only one person, or one per age, is saved or damned, which conflicts with the general warning to everyone.
[BINTSHATI:v2p115/r6] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | holds | Al-atqa is unrestricted here, unlike atqakum in 49:13, which is qualified by reference to the people addressed. | mentions 49:13
[BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | holds | The oath's night, daylight, and creation frame divergent earthly endeavors, then contrasting afterlife fates: the denier's fire and the pious giver's satisfaction.
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | holds | The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17. | mentions 92:5, 92:6, 92:7, 92:8, 92:9, 92:10, 92:11, 92:17, 92:18, 92:19, 92:20
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | holds | The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct. | mentions 92:5, 92:6, 92:7, 92:8, 92:9, 92:10, 92:11, 92:14, 92:15, 92:16, 92:17, 92:18, 92:19, 92:20
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | holds | The moral opposition is now named directly through the labels al-ašqā for the damned and al-atqā for the pious.
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | holds | The longer, central portrait of the pious clarifies that generosity is for ethical purification, not repayment of worldly favors, and is directed toward the Lord's face through a biblical metaphor.
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:17:anmerkung/r1] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | holds | The phrase parallels 87:11, and atqā derives from taqwā or ittaqā as discussed for verse 5. | mentions 87:11, 92:5
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | holds | The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Verses 15–21 explain the traits of those cast into Hell and those shielded from it, together with their reward.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The warning addresses Quraysh: persistent deniers of truth face the blazing fire, while those who spend to attain purity are protected from it.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The contrast is between rejecters of God’s Messengers and believers, not degrees of wickedness or piety; conclusive warning leaves Messenger-rejecters no legitimate excuse, making them the most wretched.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Those who heed the Messenger’s warnings, prepare for judgment, and spend to cleanse their wealth are Godfearing; the earliest companions earned the rare ranks of foremost and nearest.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · some people | reports | Some infer that only the most wretched enter Hell and less-wretched people are spared.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r3] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | rejects | That inference fails in context; carried through consistently, it would wrongly imply that only the most pious are spared Hell or admitted to Paradise.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Müfessirler | reports | Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | A pious believer need not receive a favor or gain before helping; all blessings come from God, and good should be done for God's approval alone.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r6] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Taqwa derives from protecting oneself against great danger; in Qur'anic usage it chiefly means avoiding evil and doing good to protect oneself from Hell.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | After warning of the blazing fire in verse 14, verses 17–20 describe giving for God's sake without owing anyone, spiritual purification, and being kept from the fire.
[STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | Giving charity in God's name purifies both the giver and the wealth; tazakkā shares an etymological root with zakāh.
[STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4] STUDYQURAN · others | reports | Others say vv. 17–21 praise Abū Bakr, who bought and freed weak slaves; when his father asked why he did not buy stronger defenders, he said he sought no defense.
[STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5] STUDYQURAN · author | reports | One revelation account says Bilāl was tortured after desecrating the Kaʿbah idols, kept testifying to God's oneness, and the Prophet assured him that the One would save him.
